tasks.gr9-diary-entry-t2: Topic: Writing a diary entry for Grade 9 English Home Language (CAPS Grade 9 term 2 transactional text). Cover that a diary entry is a portrayal of daily events with the writer's evaluation of the day or event, written from the writer's point of view in the first person, with the date at the top, events in order, simple language that is to the point, a tone set by the nature of the entry, tenses (past for events, present for feelings, future for plans), and the writing process (plan, draft, revise, edit, proof-read). Ask learners to recognise features, spot sentences that do or do not suit a diary entry, and choose suitable tone and tense.
tasks.gr9-constitution-and-policy-t2: Topic: Writing a constitution and a policy for Grade 9 English Home Language (CAPS Grade 9 term 2 transactional text). Cover that a constitution is a set of fundamental principles or rules that governs an organisation (a stokvel, burial society, youth organisation or soccer club), that the rules are agreed, binding and can be amended, the parts (name, aims or terms of reference, membership, meetings, amendments, date of adoption, signature), numbered clauses in formal, exact, impersonal language (must for a duty, may for a permission), and how a policy deals with one matter. Ask learners to recognise parts and features, choose suitable language and tell a constitution from a policy.
tasks.gr9-will-and-testament-t3: Topic: Reading and writing a will and testament for Grade 9 English Home Language (CAPS Grade 9 term 3 transactional text). Cover the key words (testator, estate, beneficiary, executor), the parts of a will (title and testator, executor, beneficiaries, the rest of the estate, date and signatures), the formal and exact language of a will (present tense, full names, numbered clauses, nothing vague), the execution of the will (signing, with witnesses who saw the testator sign) and the writing process. Keep to the school-task level: do not ask about the details of the law on valid wills (ages, number of witnesses) and treat a real will as something to be drawn up with a lawyer. Ask learners to recognise parts and key words and to choose exact, formal wording.
tasks.gr9-cv-and-covering-letter-t3: Topic: Writing a CV and a covering letter for Grade 9 English Home Language (CAPS Grade 9 term 3 transactional text). Cover that a CV presents the writer to the world with a strong first impression, is clear, objective and concise, addresses the post applied for, and provides personal details, formal qualifications, work experience (if applicable) and referees; and the covering letter (formal letter layout: sender's address, date, receiver's address, salutation, subject line, short paragraphs, closing with Yours faithfully after Dear Sir or Madam and Yours sincerely after a name), its link to the CV and the writing process. Ask learners to recognise parts, choose suitable wording and choose the correct closing.
tasks.gr9-letter-of-application-t4: Topic: Writing a letter of application for Grade 9 English Home Language (CAPS Grade 9 term 4 formal letter). Cover the purpose (asking for a post, place or bursary and showing why you suit it), the layout of a formal letter (the writer's and the recipient's address, date, formal salutation after the recipient's address, an underlined subject line after the salutation, introduction, body and conclusion, a formal closing followed by the writer's surname and initials, Yours faithfully after Dear Sir or Madam and Yours sincerely after a name), what goes in each paragraph, formal register and the writing process. Ask learners to recognise layout and parts and to choose suitable formal wording.
tasks.gr9-email-t4: Topic: Writing an e-mail for Grade 9 English Home Language (CAPS Grade 9 term 4 transactional text). Cover the purpose (to inform and to maintain a relationship), the parts (the recipient's address as name, server and country, for example moloi.q@webmail.co.za; CC for people whose attention is called to the e-mail; the subject as a summary of the content; the message; the sender's name and signature; the sender's address appears automatically), formal and informal register and greetings and closings, correct format, main and supporting ideas, logical order and the writing process. Ask learners to recognise parts and choose suitable register.
